An Apple billboard in Italy featuring a young child holding an iPhone has drawn criticism, prompting the country's child rights watchdog to refer the ad to three regulatory bodies. Here are the details.

Apple's 'Relax, it's iPhone' ad campaign has drawn criticism in Italy

Italy's Authority for Children and Adolescents (AGIA) has expressed concern over a billboard set up by Apple in Milan showing a young child holding an iPhone, with the slogan 'Tutto ok, è iPhone'.

The ad is part of Apple's long-running 'Relax, it's iPhone' campaign, which typically shows iPhones surviving various potentially damaging scenarios.

The latest billboards in the series show the iPhone being used in heavy rain, being knocked off a table by a cat, and being carried in a dog's mouth.

One of the new billboards features a young child holding an iPhone, presumably intended to convey that parents need not worry even if a toddler drops the device. However, the composition has sparked controversy over what AGIA describes as the 'normalisation of electronic babysitters'.

AGIA said in a press release that the matter was brought to its attention by a Milan resident, who described the image as 'disturbing' because it 'brings together two worlds that should remain separate'.

AGIA said it has referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian Competition Authority AGCM, and the country's advertising self-regulatory body IAP 'for appropriate scrutiny and any necessary action'.

Apple has not yet publicly responded to the matter.
